test_title: PYST 5: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: In a zoo, there are horse and pigeons. If heads are counted, there are 340 heads and if legs are counted there are 1060 legs. How many pigeons are there?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of pigeons (2-legged) = (4 × Total Heads − Total Legs) ÷ 2

Given: Heads = 340, Legs = 1060

Pigeons = (4 × 340 − 1060) ÷ 2

Pigeons = (1360 − 1060) ÷ 2 = 300 ÷ 2 = 150

**∴ The correct answer is 150 pigeons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total heads = 340, Total legs = 1060

Formula Used: Alligation Method or Linear Equations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/382a2964a9b18644efa8cbbc6dbaa0ce3805ea871486ed2a65cd24906b0ccf10.png] 

⇒ Let the number of pigeons be P and horses be H.

⇒ P + H = 340 (Equation 1)

⇒ 2P + 4H = 1060 (Equation 2)

⇒ Multiply Equation 1 by 2: 2P + 2H = 680

⇒ Subtract this from Equation 2: (2P + 4H) − (2P + 2H) = 1060 − 680

⇒ 2H = 380 ⇒ H = 190

⇒ P = 340 − 190 = 150

**∴ The correct answer is 150 pigeons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Head and Leg Rule for 4-legged animals

Number of 4-legged animals = (Legs ÷ 2) − Heads. This is a direct variation of the linear equation method.

Alligation Method

Ratio of two groups = (Value₂ − Mean) : (Mean − Value₁), where Mean is the average value per unit.

Logic for 2-legged animals

If all N animals were 4-legged, total legs would be 4N. The difference (4N − Actual Legs) ÷ 2 gives the number of 2-legged animals.</p
